ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r13.claim: Al-nadī and al-nādī mean a gathering place for an event or consultation; it can also be the generous people's assembly or simply a meeting with people present. A line by Ḥātim illustrates the word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r13.anchor: الندي والنادي: المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه لحادثة أو مشورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r8.claim: The verse about clear signs was revealed concerning al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith and his companions: poor Companions wore rough clothes while polytheists groomed their hair and wore fine silk and clothes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r8.anchor: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات نزلت في النضر بن الحارث وأصحابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r9.claim: They asked which faction had the better home and gathering, assuming worldly comfort showed God's favor; the author links this taunt to the preceding proof about resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r9.anchor: فقالوا للمؤمنين: أي الفريقين خير مقاما أي منزلا وسكنا وأحسن نديا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r10.speaker: أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r10.claim: They read yutlā in masculine form; the majority read feminine tatlā, since believers recited the Qur'an to unbelievers and praised the Prophet's signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن يتلى بالياء والجمهور بالتاء من فوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r11.claim: The unbelievers argued that God favors His beloved people, then pointed to their own wealth and fine appearance as proof they were better than the poor believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p289/r11.anchor: إنما يحسن الله لأحب الخلق إليه وينعم على أهل الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r1.claim: Bayyināt may mean carefully ordered wording and concise meaning, manifest miraculousness, or proofs; the adjective reinforces a quality always true of God's signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r1.anchor: ومعنى بينات مرتلات الألفاظ ملخصات المعاني أو ظاهرات الإعجاز أو حججا وبراهين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r2.claim: The majority read maqāman with fatḥa; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ḥamīd and others read it with ḍamma. Either vowel allows a verbal noun or a place of standing/residence, and the word is accusative of specification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور مقاما بفتح الميم. وقرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wealthy opponents wrongly infer from their worldly status that their beliefs and deeds are superior, deny the Judgment, and assume they would remain better off if it came; God refutes this reasoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They contended that if they were well-off in relation to the believers of the Qur’ān, it necessarily means that their beliefs and deeds were also better

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The rejecters think their superior worldly rank proves they are more guided and expect their status to continue after death through intercessors and partners of God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regard themselves to be more guided and if ever there is going to be a Judgement Day they will have this same status through the help of their intercessors and partners of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wrongdoers argue that their superior worldly status proves God favors them more than believers and so they should not expect divine wrath or punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: since in this world they have a superior status, why should they think that they deserve the wrath of God

BURSEVI:v5p270/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270/r1.claim: The Quranic signs are clear in miraculous proof and meaning; the disbelievers are Nadr ibn al-Harith and companions addressing poor believers.
BURSEVI:v5p270/r1.anchor: واضحات الاعجاز والمعاني وهي حال مؤكدة فإن آيات الله لا ينفك عنها الوضوح

BURSEVI:v5p270/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270/r2.claim: The lām may mark speech addressed to believers or spoken about them; maqam means residence and nadi a council gathering leaders and supporters.
BURSEVI:v5p270/r2.anchor: أي : لفقراء المؤمنين واللام للتبليغ كما في مثل قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v5p270/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270/r3.claim: The disbelievers groomed and perfumed themselves, boasted of worldly prosperity over poor believers, and argued true faith would bring better worldly conditions to divert them from religion.
BURSEVI:v5p270/r3.anchor: قالوا مفتخرين بالحظوظ الدنيوية على فقراء المؤمنين لو كنتم على الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.claim: The passage reports what the polytheists said after hearing signs exposing their shameful state and outcome; the signs include the preceding verses and are clear either in miraculous inimitability or in wording, meaning, and explained purposes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r1.anchor: إلى اخرها حكاية لما قالوا عند سماع الآيات الناعية عليهم فظاعة حالهم ووخامة ما لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers بَيِّنَات as a circumstantial qualifier that reinforces the whole statement, despite the clause not having two nominal parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r2.anchor: والوجه كما في الكشاف أن يكون ( بينات ) حالا مؤكدة لمضمون الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة، الأعرج، ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.claim: They read وإذا يتلى with a masculine verb because آيات is metaphorically feminine and separated from the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن ( وإذا يتلى ) بالياء التحتية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.claim: The relative description الذين كفروا highlights that their statement came from people rejecting the revelation, or specifically hardened leaders such as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his followers, about whom the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r4.anchor: ووضع الموصول موضع الضمير للتنبيه على أنهم قالوا ما قالوا كافرين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r5.claim: The ل in للذين آمنوا is communicative, as in telling someone something; a causal reading, for their sake or about them, is less fitting because the question compares both groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله تعالى ( للذين آمنوا ( للتبليغ كما في قلت له كذا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r6.claim: أي الفريقين means which group, us or you, has the better place; مقام broadly denotes residence or location, while the nominative reading can suggest a place of dwelling.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r6.anchor: كانهم قالوا : اينا ( خير ( نحن اوانتم ( مقاما ( أي مكانا ومنزلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r7.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن محيصن، حميد، الجعفي، أبو حاتم عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r7.claim: They read مقاما with a damma on the م, from إقامة, meaning a place of residence; it agrees in sense with the open-vowel reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد والجعفي وابوا حاتم عن أبى عمرو ( مقاما ) بضم الاميم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r8.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r8.claim: Al-Bahr allows both vowelings to be verbal nouns, respectively from قام and أقام.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r8.anchor: وجوز في البحر احتمال المفتوح والمضموم للمصدرية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r9.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r9.claim: A distinction attributed to Abu al-Su'ud makes the open form any place of standing, temporary or lasting, while the damma form is where one is established by another or remains for an extended time.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r9.anchor: وهو أن الأول يعنى المفتوح الميم موضع قيام الشئ اعم من أن يكون قيامه فيه بنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r10.claim: When a quadriliteral verb specifically means an externally established or enduring place, the damma form is the required one.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p124#2/r10.anchor: وأما إذا قصد ذلك فان مقتضاه الثاني كما إذا قلت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r1.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r1.claim: The account distinguishes original lexical standing from later usage: the former is a place something stands by itself, while the latter is like a necessary station for a volitional being; with a quadriliteral verb, a verbal noun takes damma.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r1.anchor: ومقامات الكلمات كلها وان كانت منوطه بوضع الوضع لكن مفامها المنوط باصل الوضع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r2.claim: The text concludes that مقام in this verse is a tamyiz, not an adverbial or verbal noun; its sense is which group's position is better.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r2.anchor: وانت تعلم أنه في هذا المقام ليس منصوبا على الظرفية ولا على المصدرية بل منصوب على التمييز

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r3.claim: نديا means a council or gathering; al-Bahr specifies a meeting for discussion or consultation, while another view connects it with generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r3.anchor: أي مجلسا ومجتمعا وفي البحر هو المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه لحادثه أو مشورة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r4.claim: The unbelievers reportedly groomed and perfumed themselves, wore their finest clothes, and taunted poor believers with their superior social setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r4.anchor: يروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنوها ويتطيبون ويلبسون مفاخر الملابس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r5.claim: Al-Razi explains their argument: if believers were right, a wise God would not leave His sincere allies in hardship while disbelievers enjoyed comfort; the inference is invalid and based on a foolish view, as the next verse refutes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125/r5.anchor: قال الأمام : ومرادهم من ذلك معارضت المؤمنين كانهم قالوا لوا كنتم على الحق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r1.claim: The disbelievers are al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and other Quraysh; believers are the Prophet's poor companions, whose rough living and clothes contrasted with idolaters' groomed hair, oil, and silk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r1.anchor: يعني: النضر بن الحارث وذويه من قريش {للذين آمنوا} يعني فقراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r2.claim: Maqām means residence and dwelling; Ibn Kathir's reading with ḍamma means staying or residence.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir reads مقاما with ḍamma on the mīm, meaning residence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r3.anchor: ابن كثير: " مقاما " بضم الميم أي إقامة]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r4.claim: Nadi means an assembly or gathering place.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r1.claim: The signs are clear in wording, meaning, and inimitability; “better station” means a place to stand or reside, with Ibn Kathir reading residence, while assembly means gathering.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r1.anchor: مرتلات الألفاظ مبينات المعاني بنفسها أو ببيان الرسول

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r2.claim: Unable to challenge revelation, unbelievers boast of worldly advantages as proof of merit; the passage answers and threatens them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:73/r2.anchor: أخذوا في الافتخار بما لهم من حظوظ الدنيا والاستدلال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r3.claim: The signs are clear, whether intrinsically decisive or explained by decisive verses or the Prophet; their status is either emphatic or explanatory.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r3.anchor: أو متشابهات قد تبعها البيان بالمحكمات

BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r4.claim: Rather than assess the proofs, disbelievers use worldly abundance to taunt believers about which side has the better residence and assembly; they mistake prosperity for divine approval and ignore God’s power to remove it.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqām with a ḍamma, meaning a place of standing or assembly, while the other readers use a fatḥa.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p552/r5.anchor: على قراءة ابن كثير بضم الميم والجماعة بفتحها

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r1.claim: When Quranic signs are recited, the unbelievers answer with rejection and stubborn deviation, yet claim rightness on conjecture and suspicion.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r1.anchor: قابلوها بالرد والجحد والعتو والزيغ ، ويدعون أنهم على حق ، ولا يعتمدون في ذلك إلا على الحدس والظن

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r2.claim: They follow the path of earlier deniers in doubt and will meet what their bad deeds warrant.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r2.anchor: ينخرطون في سلك من تقدمهم ، كما سلكوا في الريب منهاجهم ، وسيلقون ما يستوجبونه على سوء أعمالهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r3.claim: God gives disbelievers respite so they trust false conjectures and mistake their apparent well-being for security, then His decree overtakes them according to their assumptions.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r3.anchor: يمهل الكفار ليركنوا إلى أباطيل ظنونهم ، ويغتروا بسلامة أحوالهم ، فينسونه في غفلة الإمهال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r1.claim: The verse presents another form of worldly delusion: polytheists judged divine favor by comfort and status, boasting over believers of modest means and claiming they would follow only if the poor were expelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r1.anchor: وهذا صنف آخر من غرور المشركين بالدنيا وإناطتهم دلالة على السعادة بأحوال طيب العيش في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r2.claim: The Prophet recited Quranic warnings and promises, but the polytheists argued that true believers would already enjoy worldly prosperity; the clear verses instead supplied compelling proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r2.anchor: كان النبي يقرأ على المشركين القرآن فيسمعون آيات النعي عليهم وإنذارهم بسوء المصير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r3.claim: Their taunt echoes the claim that disbelievers came to faith only after the believers, cited in 46:11; their class-based argument also recalls the rebuke in 6:52–53.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r3.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا لو كان خيرا ما سبقونا إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r4.claim: Tilāwa means recitation; the Qur’anic verses are bayyināt because their proof is clear and filled with persuasive evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r4.anchor: والتلاوة : القراءة . وقد تقدمت عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r5.claim: The lām before “those who believe” may mean “on account of them,” making this a private remark among the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله { للذين آمنوا } يجوز كونها للتعليل ، أي قالوا لأجل الذين آمنوا ، أي من أجل شأنهم ، فيكون هذا قول المشركين فيما بينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r6.claim: Alternatively, the lām may mark the object governed by “they said,” making the polytheists address the believers directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p153/r6.anchor: ويجوز كونها متعلقة بفعل { قال } لتعديته إلى متعلقه ، فيكون قولهم خطابا منهم للمؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r1.claim: Their question about which faction is better is confirmatory: they expect their worldly advantage to establish their superiority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r1.anchor: والاستفهام في قولهم { أي الفريقين } تقريري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce maqāman with fatḥa, a place noun from “stand,” metaphorically denoting rank and prominence, as in 55:46.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r2.anchor: وقرأ من عدا ابن كثير { مقاما } بفتح الميم على أنه اسم مكان من قام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqāman with ḍamma, from “reside,” meaning a better worldly life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r3.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير بضم الميم من أقام بالمكان ، وهو مستعمل في الكون في الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r1.speaker: الأعرج وابن محيصن وأبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r1.claim: These readers read yutlā with a lower yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r1.anchor: قرأ الأعرج وابن محيصن وأبو حيوة «يتلى» بالياء من تحت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r2.claim: Quraysh argued that God favors those He loves, pointing to their wealth and fine appearance while believers were poor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r2.anchor: كان الكافر منهم يقول إن الله إنما يحسن لأحب الخلق إليه وإنما ينعم على أهل الحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read maqāman with fatḥa; it can mean a verbal noun or place, but context selects place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «مقاما» بفتح الميم ولا مقام لكم [الأحزاب: 13] بالفتح أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqāman with ḍamma, from aqāma, which can also yield a verbal noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «مقاما» بضم الميم وهو ظرف من أقام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.claim: Ubayy reads maqāmin with ḍamma in the phrase in Sūrat al-Dukhān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي في مقام أمين [الدخان: 51] بضم الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.claim: These readers pronounce all the cited forms with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم جميعهن بالفتح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads lā maqāma lakum with ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم «لا مقام لكم» بالضم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.claim: Al-nadī and al-nādī mean an assembly where people gather; Ḥātim's poetry witnesses the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.anchor: و «الندي» والنادي المجلس فيه الجماعة ومنه قول حاتم الطائي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r1.claim: The speakers are the Quraysh idolaters addressing poor believers; they boast about their own dwellings and meeting places.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r1.anchor: يعني المشركين آياتنا يعني القرآن قال الذين كفرا يعني المشركي قريش للذين آمنوا أي لفقراء المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r2.claim: These readers pronounce مقام with a fatḥa on mīm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر وحفص عن عاصم مقاما بفتح الميم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir pronounces مقام with a ḍamma on mīm; al-Farisi says both forms mean a place of residence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بضم الميم قال أبو علي الفارسي المقام اسم المثوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ says nadī and nādī are two dialect forms for a gathering or assembly.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r5.claim: They ask which party is better, boasting of their homes and social assemblies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p257#3/r5.anchor: ومعنى الكلام أنحن خير أم أنتم فافتخروا عليهم بالمساكن والمجالس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r1.claim: Disbelievers turn away from clear proofs and boast they have better homes and fuller, more frequented councils, arguing this worldly standing proves their religion true despite believers' hidden meeting places.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r1.anchor: ويقولون عن الذين آمنوا مفتخرين عليهم ومحتجين على صحة ما هم عليه من الدين الباطل بأنهم: {خير مقاما وأحسن نديا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains maqam as home, nadi as council, athath as belongings, and r'iy as appearance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {خير مقاما وأحسن نديا} قال: المقام: المنزل، والندي: المجلس، والأثاث: المتاع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r4.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's gloss of maqam as residence and nadi as meeting place, prosperity, and pleasure; he links the terms to Pharaoh and Lot's people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r4.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: المقام: المسكن، والندي: المجلس والنعمة والبهجة التي كانوا فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r5.claim: Qatada says polytheists mocked Muhammad's companions for rough living and appearance by asking which group had better homes and assemblies; Mujahid and al-Dahhak agree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: لما رأوا أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في عيشهم خشونة، وفيهم قشافة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p263/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p263/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p263/r3.claim: The contrast in the gathering recalls the earlier boast about which group had a better dwelling and council.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p263/r3.anchor: وهاهنا يقال: {أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا}

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r6.claim: Nadī is a gathering place, synonymous with nādī; Dār al-Nadwa in Mecca was Quraysh's council hall.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r6.anchor: والندي: المجلس الذي قد اجتمع فيه أهله

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r7.claim: Nadawtu al-qawma means I gathered the people in an assembly.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r7.anchor: ندوت القوم أندوهم ندوا إذا جمعتهم في مجلس

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r8.claim: A poet's line uses nadā for generous company.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: ودعيت في أولي الندى

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r14.claim: Nadiyyan is an accusative of specification.

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r16.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r16.claim: The passage about unbelievers boasting was reportedly revealed concerning al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith and Quraysh challenging poor Muslims.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r16.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: وإذا تتلى عليهم ... الآية. في النضر بن الحارث

JISHUMI:v6p4600/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r9.claim: Unbelievers boasted of worldly status and judged the afterlife by present wealth; that is no proof of their final outcome.
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r9.anchor: وإنما تفاخروا بالمال وزينة الدنيا ولم يتفكروا في العاقبة

JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.claim: Worldly wealth and leadership cannot benefit a person at the Resurrection, as destroyed nations show.
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن المال والرئاسة في الدنيا لا يغني عنه شيئا يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r11.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r11.claim: Al-Aṣamm connects the verse to the description of unbelievers when clear revelations are recited: recitation increases the believer in guidance.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r11.anchor: يتصل بقوله: (وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات) كأنه قيل: إذا يتلى القرآن فالذين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.claim: “Clear” may mean well-articulated wording, concise meanings, evident aims, decisive or explained ambiguous verses, clarification by the Prophet, miracles, or proofs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r1.anchor: مرتلات الألفاظ ، ملخصات المعاني : مبينات المقاصد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.claim: The strongest parsing treats “clear” as an emphatic circumstantial description, since God's signs are necessarily clear proofs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r2.anchor: لأن آيات الله لا تكون إلا واضحة وحججا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.claim: Speaking “to the believers” can mean addressing them directly or speaking for their sake, as in the parallel about unbelievers' claims.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r3.anchor: وأنهم يفوهون به لأجلهم وفي معناهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqāman with ḍamma for a residence or home; the other reading with fatḥ means a place of standing; both mean location.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r5.claim: Nadī is the gathering place or assembly of a people, where they meet.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.claim: Ignorant of more than worldly appearances, the disbelievers use prosperity as their measure of truth, asking which team has the better place and assembly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r6.anchor: من المؤمنين بالآيات والجاحدين لها أوفر حظا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.claim: A report says they groomed, oiled, perfumed, and adorned themselves, boasting to poor Muslims that they were more honored by God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p37#2/r7.anchor: يروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنون ويتطيبون ويتزينون بالزين الفاخرة

FARRA:v2p170/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r7.claim: Maqāman means an assembly, and nadī and nādī are dialect variants.
FARRA:v2p170/r7.anchor: وقوله: خير مقاما وأحسن نديا [73] : مجلسا. والندي والنادي لغتان.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r1.claim: Maqaman may mean a dwelling in Paradise or Hell, a disputation about whose case prevails through obedience or is defeated by sin, or the place of judgment; Thaʿlab distinguishes residence with damma from assembly with fatḥa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r1.anchor: أحدهما : منزل إقامة في الجنة أو النار . والثاني : يعني كلام قائم بجدل واحتجاج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r2.claim: Nadiyyan may mean a better assembly or more spacious life; another possibility locates residence in Paradise or Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أفضل مجلسا . الثاني : أوسع عيشا . ويحتمل ثالثا

MUJAHID:v1p389/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p389/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p389/r1.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh taunted Muhammad's companions about which group had the better dwelling and meeting place; al-nadi means assemblies.
MUJAHID:v1p389/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا ﴾ قال قريش تقوله لأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والندي المجالس

MUQATIL:19:73-74/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r1.claim: When the clear Qur'an is recited, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAlqama and other disbelievers boast to believers, wearing fine clothes with oiled hair, and ask which group has better status and housing in Mecca.
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r1.anchor: يعني القرآن، { بينات } ، يعني واضحات، { قال الذين كفروا } ، وهم النضر بن الحارث بن علقمة وغيره

MUQATIL:19:73-74/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r2.claim: Maqāman means a place to live, as in 'a noble residence'; nadiyyan means an assembly, as in the verse about wrongdoing in one's gathering.
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r2.anchor: يعني أفضل مقاما للمساكن من مساكن مكة، ومثله في حم الدخان:

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r1.claim: The recited signs are manifest in miraculousness or in proofs and arguments; this is emphatic because God's signs are necessarily clear proofs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r1.anchor: ظاهرات الاعجاز أو حججا وبراهين حال مؤكدة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r2.claim: The unbelievers are the Quraysh polytheists, who groomed their hair and affected elaborate dress.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r2.anchor: أي مشركو قريش وقد رجلوا شعورهم وتكلفوا في زيهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r3.claim: The believers addressed are the poor, with disheveled hair and coarse clothes.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r4.claim: The unbelievers ask which party— themselves or the believers—has the better dwelling and gathering place.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r4.anchor: أي الفريقين ﴾ نحن أم أنتم ﴿ خير مقاما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r5.claim: مقاما with fatḥa means place of standing, hence location or home; Meccan recitation with ḍamma means residence or dwelling.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r5.anchor: بالفتح وهو موضع القيام والمراد المكان والمسكن وبالضم مكي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r6.claim: A ندي is a council where people gather to deliberate.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r7.claim: Rather than consider the manifest evidence, they boast of wealth, money, and attractive homes and circumstances.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45/r7.anchor: إذا أنزلنا آية فيها دلائل وبراهين أعرضوا عن التدبر فيها إلى الافتخار بالثروة والمال وحسن المنزل والحال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r1.claim: Maqāman means a dwelling or lodging.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r2.claim: Nadiyyan means an assembly or council; Dār al-Nadwah was named for the house where polytheists met to deliberate about the Messenger.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p275#2/r2.anchor: {وأحسن نديا} أي مجلسا. يقال للمجلس: ندي ونادي. ومنه قيل: دار الندوة، للدار التي كان المشركون يجلسون فيها ويتشاورون في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

MAJAZ:v2p9/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p9/r4.claim: نديا means a gathering or assembly and is equivalent to النادي; Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī’s line attests it, and its plural is أندية.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r4.anchor: «وأحسن نديا» (73) أي مجلسا والندى والنادي واحد ، قال حاتم طيى

MAJAZ:v2p9/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p9/r5.claim: Salāma ibn Jandal’s line uses أندية for gatherings or assemblies.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r5.anchor: والجميع منها أندية، قال سلامة بن جندل: يومان يوم مقامات وأندية

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r1.claim: The people addressed are disbelievers already mentioned in 19:66 and 19:72; worldly status is their answer to Qurʾānic recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r1.anchor: على الكفار الذين سبق ذكرهم في قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r2.claim: They use wealth and stronger support as proof of religious truth to sow doubt among the vulnerable, overlooking poor unbelievers and rich Muslims; God keeps His friends from worldly delusion.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r2.anchor: وغرضهم إدخال الشبهة على المستضعفين وإيهامهم أن من كثر ماله دل ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r3.claim: “Clear” may mean well-articulated words, concise meanings, and evident purposes; or ambiguous verses clarified by decisive ones or the Prophet’s words and deeds; or manifest inimitable signs and proofs.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r3.anchor: مرتلات الألفاظ، ملخصة المعاني، مبينات المقاصد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī takes “clear” as an emphatic circumstantial description: God’s verses are necessarily lucid proofs, as 2:91 similarly calls the Book the truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r4.anchor: والوجه أن تكون حالا مؤكدة كقوله تعالى: وهو الحق مصدقا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r5.claim: The unbelievers are Quraysh polytheists, especially al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and companions; the believers are the Prophet’s poor Companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r5.anchor: يريد مشركي قريش النضر بن الحارث وأصحابه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r6.claim: The believers’ rough appearance and worn clothes contrasted with the polytheists’ groomed hair, oiled heads, and fine clothes.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r6.anchor: وكانت فيهم قشافة، وفي عيشهم خشونة، وفي ثيابهم رثاثة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد وشبل بن عباد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r7.claim: These readers pronounce “maqāman” with ḍamma, meaning a residence or the verbal noun “residing.”
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد وشبل بن عباد «مقاما» بضم الميم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r8.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r8.claim: The other readers pronounce it with fatḥa, meaning a home or place for conducting important affairs, hence greater prestige and supporters.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “nadī” as an assembly and also as outward appearance; lexically it is a meeting and conversation place.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r9.anchor: «وأحسن نديا» أي مجلسا عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r10.claim: Dar al-Nadwa was named for Quraysh’s council there; “nādāhu” means to sit with someone in the gathering. The cited line illustrating “unādī” appears in the next source segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:73/r10.anchor: ومنه دار الندوة لأن المشركين كانوا يتشاورون فيها في أمورهم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r1.claim: A poetic line about calling the families of al-Walīd and Jaʿfar illustrates “unādī” in the sense of assembly or meeting.

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r1.claim: The Quraysh polytheists argued that if the believers were right, their worldly life should be better; a wise God would not abase devoted allies and favor those who turn away, so the reverse worldly fortunes supposedly disproved the believers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r1.anchor: لو كنتم أنتم على الحق وكنا على الباطل لكان حالكم في الدنيا أحسن وأطيب من حالنا

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r2.claim: It is reported that the unbelievers adorned their hair and clothes, perfumed themselves, then boasted to poor Muslims that they were more honored by God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r2.anchor: ويروى أنهم كانوا يرجلون شعورهم ويدهنون ويتطيبون

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r3.claim: One reading of bayyināt is articulated wording with clear meanings, either decisive verses or ambiguous ones clarified by decisive verses or by the Prophet's speech or actions.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r3.anchor: أنها مرتلات الألفاظ مبينات المعاني إما محكمات أو متشابهات فقد تبعها البيان بالمحكمات

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that the verses are manifestly miraculous: they challenged opponents, who could not produce a rival.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r4.anchor: أنها ظاهرات الإعجاز تحدى بها فما قدروا على معارضتها

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r5.claim: A third explanation takes them as plain proofs admitting no question or objection, like the proof of resurrection in this surah.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r5.anchor: دلائل ظاهرة واضحة لا يتوجه عليها سؤال ولا اعتراض مثل قوله تعالى في إثبات صحة الحشر

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir reads maqāman with ḍamma, meaning a place of residence or dwelling.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير : { مقاما } بالضم وهو موضع الإقامة والمنزل

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r7.claim: The other readers use fatḥa, taking maqāman as a place of standing.

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r8.claim: Nadī means an assembly or gathering place; its forms include nadī and nādī and its plural is andiyah, as in two cited verses.

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r9.claim: The verb nadawtu means I gathered people in the assembly; Dar al-Nadwa in Mecca was so named because people assembled there.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#2/r9.anchor: ويقال : ندوت القوم أندوهم إذا جمعتهم في المجلس

STUDYQURAN:19:73/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:73/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:73/r1.claim: In the Makkan setting, disbelievers are Quraysh idolaters and believers are the Prophet's Companions; Quraysh boast of better homes and more prominent associates, assuming earthly advantages will persist in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:19:73/r1.anchor: The Makkan idolaters boast of their being better in station

NAHHAS:v3p25/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r7.claim: The phrase is accusative of specification, as is نَدِيًّا.

TAB-FULL:v15p607/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r1.claim: The unbelieving Quraysh taunt Muhammad's believers by asking which group has better residences, more comfort, and finer, larger gatherings.
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r1.anchor: قال الذين كفروا بالله وبكتابه وآياته، وهم قريش للذين آمنوا فصدقوا به، وهم أصحاب محمد

TAB-FULL:v15p607/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r2.claim: Maqām means the place of residence; nadī is a council or gathering, and nadī and nādī have the same sense.
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r2.anchor: يعني بالمقام: موضع إقامتهم، وهي مساكنهم ومنازلهم {وأحسن نديا} [مريم: 73] وهو المجلس

TAB-FULL:v15p607/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r3.claim: The verb nadawtu means gathering people in a council; the poet Ḥātim's line uses nadī for such a gathering.
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r3.anchor: يقال منه: ندوت القوم أندوهم ندوا: إذا جمعتهم في مجلس، ويقال: هو في ندي قومه

TAB-FULL:v15p607/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses maqām as a home and nadī as a council.
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {خير مقاما وأحسن نديا} [مريم: 73] قال: المقام: المنزل، والندي: المجلس

TAB-FULL:v15p607/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also associates maqām with dwelling and its prosperity, and nadī with the meeting place, linking the wording to Pharaoh's former prosperity and Lot's assembly.
TAB-FULL:v15p607/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا} [مريم: 73] قال: المقام: المسكن،

TAB-FULL:v15p610/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses nadī as a council or meeting place.
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {وأحسن نديا} [مريم: 73] يقول: مجلسا

TAB-FULL:v15p610/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r2.claim: Mujāhid says Quraysh addressed Muhammad's companions and boasted of their own councils.
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {أي الفريقين} [مريم: 73] قال: قريش تقولها لأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v15p610/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r3.claim: Qatāda says the polytheists saw the companions living roughly and poorly dressed, then boasted of their own meeting places; he cites the call to one's council.
TAB-FULL:v15p610/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا} [مريم: 73]

TAB-FULL:v15p615#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p615#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p615#2/r2.claim: At that point the contest over which group has the better dwelling and meeting place will be settled.
TAB-FULL:v15p615#2/r2.anchor: أهم أم أنتم؟ ويتبينون حينئذ أي الفريقين خير مقاما، وأحسن نديا

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r1.claim: The disbelievers argue that the Prophet’s call cannot improve believers’ fortunes; they treat their own worldly comfort as proof that disbelief is true.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r1.anchor: وهو ردهم الدعوة النبوية بأنها لا تنفع في حسن حال المؤمنين بها شيئا ولو كانت حقة لجلبت إليهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r2.claim: Maqām means dwelling, while nadī means an assembly, possibly specifically a council for consultation.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r2.anchor: المقام اسم مكان من القيام فهو المسكن، والندي هو المجلس وقيل خصوص مجلس المشاورة

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r3.claim: The lām can mark the audience of the message or its purpose of misleading believers; the address reading better fits the context.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r3.anchor: للتبليغ كما قيل، وقيل تفيد معنى التعليل أي قالوا لأجل الذين آمنوا أي لأجل إغوائهم وصرفهم عن الإيمان، والأول أنسب للسياق

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r4.claim: The pronoun in عليهم refers to people generally, believers and disbelievers, with قال الذين كفروا then replacing the pronoun explicitly.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r4.anchor: دون الكفار فقط حتى يكون قوله { قال الذين كفروا } من قبيل وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r5.claim: The two groups are disbelievers and believers; disbelievers feign a question while asserting that their own dwellings and gatherings are superior.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r5.anchor: وكان مرادهم أن الكفار هم خير مقاما وأحسن نديا من المؤمنين الذين كان الغالب عليهم العبيد والفقراء لكنهم أوردوه في صورة السؤال

TABRISI:19:71-75/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:19:71-75/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads maqāman with ḍamma; others use fatḥa.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير مقاما بضم الميم والباقون بفتحها

TABRISI:19:71-75/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r3.speaker: أهل المدينة غير ورش وابن عامر والأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر
TABRISI:19:71-75/r3.claim: These readers pronounce riyyan without hamza and with doubled yāʾ; the others retain hamza.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r3.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة غير ورش وابن عامر والأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر وريا بغير همز

TABRISI:19:71-75/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r4.speaker: طلحة
TABRISI:19:71-75/r4.claim: A rare reading from Ṭalḥa has riyyan with light yāʾ and no hamza.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r4.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة طلحة وريا خفيفة بلا همز

TABRISI:19:71-75/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:19:71-75/r5.claim: A rare reading from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr uses zayyan with zāy.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r5.anchor: وقراءة سعيد بن جبير وزيا بالزاي

TABRISI:19:71-75/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71-75/r7.claim: Maqām with fatḥa can be verbal noun or place from qāma; with ḍamma it may likewise be noun or place from aqāma.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r7.anchor: فالمقام بفتح الميم يصلح أن يكون مصدرا من قام يقوم ويصلح أن يكون اسم الموضع

TABRISI:19:71-75/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r8.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:19:71-75/r8.claim: The cited line about maqāmāt means people of stations or gatherings, with ahl omitted.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r8.anchor: فإنما هو على حذف المضاف أي أهل مقامات ومشاهد

TABRISI:19:71-75/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r9.speaker: السكري
TABRISI:19:71-75/r9.claim: Al-Sukkarī distinguishes maqāma as assembly from maqām as dwelling; nadi and nādī both mean assembly.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r9.anchor: قال السكري المقامة المجلس والمقام المنزل

TABRISI:19:71-75/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71-75/r10.claim: Nadi and nādī mean a gathering place, as in the verse about wrongdoing in a gathering.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r10.anchor: فمن ذلك قوله تعالى وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر

TABRISI:19:71-75/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r11.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:19:71-75/r11.claim: Riyyan derives from raʾaytu and names what appears, not the verbal noun; the form here is the seen object.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي رؤي فعل من رأيت فكأنه اسم لما ظهر وليس المصدر

TABRISI:19:71-75/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r12.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:19:71-75/r12.claim: Doubled riyyan can derive from seeing or being well-watered; zayyan can derive from gathering and describe rich adornment.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r12.anchor: قال ابن جني من قرأ وريا مشددة فإنه فعل إما من رأيت وإما من رويت

TABRISI:19:71-75/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71-75/r13.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:19:71-75/r13.claim: A softened hamza becomes yāʾ after kasra and the resulting yāʾs assimilate; zayyan derives from z-w-y with wāw changed to yāʾ.
TABRISI:19:71-75/r13.anchor: ومن خفف الهمزة من ورئيا لزم أن يبدل منها الياء لانكسار ما قبلها

TABRISI:19:71/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71/r1.claim: A poem uses zay for beautiful attire and furnishings.
TABRISI:19:71/r1.anchor:
أهاجتك الظعائن يوم باتوا
بذي الزي الجميل من الأثاث

TABRISI:19:71/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71/r3.claim: Nadī and nādī mean a gathering place; Dār al-Nadwa was the Meccan council house where people assembled to consult.
TABRISI:19:71/r3.anchor: والندي والنادي المجلس الذي قد اجتمع فيه أهله ومنه دار الندوة

TABRISI:19:71/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71/r7.claim: Maqāman and nadiyyan are accusatives of specification; kam has an omitted counted generation clear from context.

TABRISI:19:72-75/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:72-75/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:72-75/r4.claim: Disbelievers ask believers which group has better dwelling and assembly, boasting of worldly wealth to mislead the weak into equating riches with afterlife reward.
TABRISI:19:72-75/r4.anchor: وغرضهم الإنكار أي الفريقين أي أنحن أم أنتم خير منزلا ومسكنا

THALABI:v6p228/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p228/r3.claim: The unbelievers are al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and other Quraysh; they taunt the Prophet’s poor, rough-clothed, poorly dressed followers while wearing fine clothes and grooming themselves.
THALABI:v6p228/r3.anchor: قال الذين كفروا يعني النضر بن الحرث ودونه من قريش للذين آمنوا يعني فقراء أصحاب رسول الله

THALABI:v6p228/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r4.speaker: أهل مكة
THALABI:v6p228/r4.claim: Meccan readers use maqāman with ḍamm, meaning a place or period of residence.
THALABI:v6p228/r4.anchor: وقرأ أهل مكة مقاما بالضم أي إقامة

THALABI:v6p228/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p228/r5.claim: Nadiyy means an assembly place, like a club; Dār al-Nadwa was where Quraysh sat and discussed their affairs.
THALABI:v6p228/r5.anchor: وأحسن نديا يعني مجلسا، ومثله النادي، ومنه دار الندوة لأن المشركين كانوا يجلسون فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r1.claim: The disbelievers are Quraysh polytheists speaking to poor believers; clear signs means the Qur’an, and they ask which side has the better place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وإذا تتلى عليهم} يعني: على المشركين {آياتنا بينات} يريد القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r2.claim: Both readings maqāman and maqāman denote a place or dwelling; the accusative form can be verbal noun or place noun, while the nominative form can mean residence or its location.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r2.anchor: وقرئ: مقاما بالضم (¬3). وهما المنزل والمسكن، وكذا قال المفسرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r3.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r3.claim: Maqām may denote a seat or a scene, as at 27:39; a poetic line uses it for the place where someone stands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p301/r3.anchor: قال الأخفش: (يقال للمقعد المقام وللمشهد المقام)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r1.claim: Nadi means a gathering or council, as does nadi; its root means gathering people, and the place is called a council only while its people are present.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r1.anchor: الندي فعيل بمعنى الفاعل وهو المجلس، وكذلك النادي، يقال: ندوت القوم، أندوهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r2.claim: The wording is related to 29:29 and Dar al-Nadwa, where Meccans gathered to deliberate; unādīka means I consult or sit with you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r2.anchor: ومن هذا قوله: {وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر} [العنكبوت: 29] ولذلك سميت دار الندوة بمكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r3.speaker: كثير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r3.claim: A line by Kathir uses the verb unādīka as evidence for the gathering/council sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r3.anchor: قال كثير: أناديك ما حجت حجيج وكبرت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r4.claim: The polytheists boast to poor believers about their greater status, houses, assemblies, and comfortable livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p302/r4.anchor: والمعنى: أن المشركين قالوا للفقراء المؤمنين أنحن أم أنتم أعظم شأنا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r4.claim: The clear signs are the Quran and what God explains in it; the disbelievers are Quraysh polytheists addressing believers, and the two groups are themselves versus the believers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r4.anchor: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات } يعني: القرآن وما بين الله فيه { قال الذين كفروا } يعني: مشركي قريش { للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين } منا ومنكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r5.claim: The question asks which group has the better home and gathering place; the wealthy, adorned disbelievers contrasted themselves with poor, shabby believers and claimed superior status.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:70-73/r5.anchor: خير مقاما } منزلا ومسكنا { وأحسن نديا } مجلسا، وذلك أنهم كانوا أصحاب مال وزينة من الدنيا، وكان المؤمنون أصحاب فقر ورثاثة، فقالوا لهم: نحن أعظم شأنا، وأعز مجلسا، وأكرم منزلا أم أنتم؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r3.claim: The unbelievers' question about which party is better means themselves or the believers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r4.claim: The two terms mean dwelling place and gathering place; Qatāda says the latter is a meeting council, essentially the same meaning.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r4.anchor: المقام: المسكن، والندي: المجمع. وقال قتادة: الندي، المجلس. وهو واحد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the polytheists of Quraysh address the Prophet's companions with this boast.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: يقوله مشركو قريش لهؤلاء أصحاب محمد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r6.claim: Qatāda says the Meccans saw the Prophet's companions living in hardship.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد: قال قتادة: رأوا أصحاب نبي الله في عيشهم خشونة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r1.claim: Prophets' earliest followers are often poor and weak, while wealthy and powerful rejecters belittle and oppress them; the Qur'an gives many examples.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r1.anchor: Genellikle peygamberlere ilk inananlar toplumun zayıfları ve fakirleridir. Onları inkâr edenler ise servet ve iktidar sahipleridir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r2.claim: The arrogant Quraysh argued that a good message would have come to them instead of the poor, and asked which camp had superior status, followers, and homes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r2.anchor: “Eğer bu iyi bir şey olsaydı bizi bırakıp da onlara gelmezdi!” (Ahkaf 46/11) diyerek kendilerinin daha üstün

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r3.claim: The polytheists demanded that the Prophet drive away the poor before they would listen to his message.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r3.anchor: ancak fakirleri yanından kovduğu takdirde Hz. Peygamber’in tebliğini dinleyebileceklerini bildirmişlerdir

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, with a report from Abu ʿAmr and the reading of Ibn Muhaysin, reads مقاما with ḍamma; the others use fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r1.anchor: قوله: { مقاما }: قرأ ابن كثير " مقاما " بالضم، ورويت عن أبي عمرو،

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r2.claim: With either vowel, مقاما may be a place noun or verbal noun from قام or أقام, meaning good place of standing or residence.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r2.anchor: وفي كلتا القراءتين يحتمل أن يكون اسم مكان أو اسم مصدر،

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r3.claim: الندي derives from نديو with root-final waw; الندي and النادي mean a people's gathering and meeting place, as in the verse فليدع ناديه.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r3.anchor: والندي: فعيل، أصله نديو لأن لامه واوا، يقال: ندوتهم أندوهم،

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r4.claim: Another derivation links الندي to generosity, since generous people gather there; Hatim's poem uses الندي for the gathering.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r4.anchor: والندي والنادي: مجلس القوم ومتحدثهم. وقيل: هو مشتق من الندى وهو الكرم؛

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r5.speaker: حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r5.claim: Hatim's poem provides an example of الندي meaning a gathering place.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r5.anchor:
وقال حاتم:
3251- ودعيت في أولى الندي ولم
ينظر إلي بأعين خزر

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r6.claim: مقاما and نديا are accusatives of specification after the comparative.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r6.anchor: و " مقاما " و " نديا " منصوبان على التمييز من أفعل.

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r7.claim: They read يتلى with yāʾ; the other readers use tāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة والأعرج وابن محيصن " يتلى " بالياء من تحت،

SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r8.claim: The lām in للذين most likely conveys speech, though it can express cause.
SAMIN-DURR:19:73/r8.anchor: واللام في " للذين " يحتمل أن تكون للتبليغ، وهو الظاهر، وأن تكون للتعليل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r3.claim: نديا means a gathering or meeting place.
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r3.anchor:
خير مقاما وأحسن نديا (73)
(وأحسن نديا).
معناه مجلسا

ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n58/r1.claim: The two groups are types of human society distinguished by fundamentally different approaches to faith and morality.
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n58/r1.anchor: two kinds or types of human society characterized by their fundamentally different approach to problems of faith and morality

ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r1.claim: The unbelievers' rhetorical question advances a superficially plausible but false case for societies guided by expediency instead of absolute moral duties.
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r1.anchor: a superficially plausible but intrinsically fallacious argument in favour of a society which refuses to submit to any absolute moral imperatives

ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r2.claim: Materialistic societies treat worldly power and success as proof that moral and metaphysical restraints obstruct unlimited development.
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r2.anchor: material success and power are usually seen as consequences of a more or less conscious rejection of all metaphysical considerations

ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r3.claim: Ethical restraints limit selfish power seeking but free society from destructive tensions, producing more durable social well-being.
ASAD-NOTES:19:73#n59/r3.anchor: it is these moral considerations and restraints - and they alone - that can free a community from the interminable, self-destructive inner tensions and frustrations

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r1.claim: Readers differ in the vowels of مقام at three passages; Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Hafs have selected exceptions while other transmissions open the forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير: (خير مقاما) بضم الميم وفي مقام أمين [الدخان/ 51] بفتح الميم،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r2.claim: Both form-I قام and form-IV أقام yield مقام for a verbal noun or a place; it can mean standing, residence, or location.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r2.anchor: اعلم أنهم قد قالوا: قام يقوم، وأقام يقيم، والمصدر واسم الموضع جميعا من فعل يفعل على: مفعل،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.claim: مقام can name the action or place of إقامة; مجراها and مرساها are likewise parsed as verbal nouns.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.anchor: وأما أقام يقيم فالمصدر والموضع يجيئان منه على مقام،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r4.claim: The source distinguishes a location in مقام إبراهيم from interpretations of مقام as a gathering place or scene of assembly.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r4.anchor: وقال: فيه آيات بينات مقام إبراهيم [آل عمران/ 97] فهذا على موضع قيامه، وليس المصدر.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r5.claim: In في مقام أمين, the sense is a secure dwelling place, since a place can be described as safe or fearful.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r5.anchor: وأما قوله: إن المتقين في مقام أمين [الدخان/ 51] فالمعنى على الموضع، ألا ترى أن الموضع يوصف بالأمن،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r1.claim: Hassan's line about رسوم المقام shows that the word takes the sense of a place, since ruins attach to locations rather than events.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r1.anchor: ويدل عليه أيضا قول حسان: ما هاج حسان رسوم المقام فالرسم إنما يضاف إلى الأمكنة،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r2.claim: مقامات in a poem means people of gathering places by omitted أهل; المجلس similarly can mean people gathered there, as al-Asmaʿi's verse shows.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r2.anchor: وأما قول الشاعر: وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوهها ... وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل فإنما هذا على حذف المضاف،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r3.speaker: السكري
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r3.claim: Al-Sukkari reports al-Asmaʿi's distinction: المقامة means an assembly, while المقام means a dwelling.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r3.anchor: قال السكري: المقامة المجلس والمقام: المنزل.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r4.claim: دار المقامة means a lasting residence, like دار الخلد and جنات عدن; a poem about Kufa's permanence illustrates the sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r4.anchor: فأما قوله: الذي أحلنا دار المقامة من فضله [فاطر/ 35] فهو من الإقامة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r5.claim: لا مقام لكم can mean no assembly or mustering place; the alternative vowel can mean no staying or residence, and both interpretations are possible.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r5.anchor: فأما قوله (لا مقام لكم فارجعوا) [الأحزاب/ 13] فالمعنى: لا مشهد لكم،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r6.claim: مقام may be the place where a person stands, as a rajaz line says of Ribaah's feet and the sun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p206/r6.anchor: هذا مقام قدمي رباح ... للشمس حتى دلكت براح

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.claim: For خير مقاما both vowels denote a place to dwell; النادي and الندي likewise mean an assembly, as al-Ankabut 29:29 and a line by Kathir show.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r1.anchor: فأما المقام فيمن ضم، وفيمن فتح على اسم المكان، وليس اسم الحدث، ويدل على ذلك:

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.claim: Both pronunciations of مقام are place nouns, not action nouns; the following comparison of furnishings and appearance supports a residence sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.anchor: فأما المقام فيمن ضم، وفيمن فتح على اسم المكان، وليس اسم الحدث،

IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses ḍamma mīm in khayra maqāman and fatḥa in the other two phrases; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir use ḍamma in maqāmin amīn only; Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī use fatḥa throughout. Ḥafṣ varies at al-Aḥzāb.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r2.anchor: 18 واختلفوا فى الضم والفتح للميم فى قوله ﴿ خير مقاما ﴾ 73 وفى الدخان والأحزاب

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the two groups' claims as a comparison of which has the better place and gathering.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا ﴾ قال خير مكانا وأحسن مجلسا

BURHAN:v4p170/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p170/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p170/r1.claim: The unbelievers compare the two groups' standing and gathering places; the passage exemplifies comparative خير and أحسن.
BURHAN:v4p170/r1.anchor: أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا

ITQAN:v2p349/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p349/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p349/r4.claim: نديا means a gathering place or council, supported by a poet's use of أندية.
ITQAN:v2p349/r4.anchor: قال النادي المجلس قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت الشاعر يقول

ITQAN:v2p460#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r2.claim: Ayy may be interrogative, asking which of two parties sharing a general feature is distinguished by the stated quality.
ITQAN:v2p460#2/r2.anchor: الثاني استفهامية نحو ﴿ أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا ﴾ وإنما يسأل بها عما يميز أحد المتشاركين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p145/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p145/r1.claim: Īmān linguistically means assent; in religious usage it comprises verbal profession, inward belief and tranquility, and bodily works following that assent and belief.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p145/r1.anchor: الإيمان في اللغة : التصديق . ويطلق في الشرع على ثلاثة أشياء : الإقرار باللسان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r1.speaker: البخاري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r1.claim: Al-Bukhārī glosses nadī and nādī as the same word, meaning an assembly or gathering place.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that maqām means dwelling and nadī means assembly; another report adds the blessing and pleasure they enjoyed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r2.anchor: وأسنده الطبري عن ابن عباس من عدة طرق، قال: المقام المنزل والندى المجلس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r3.speaker: قتادة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses nadī as a gathering or assembly and cites “let him call his council.”

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r4.claim: The root evokes calling and gathering; al-Jawharī restricts nadā to people assembled together, while al-Rāghib derives the names nadī, muntadā, and nadwa from meeting.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r4.anchor: وفي الندى والنادى، دلالة التنادي والتجمع، وهي أصل في المادة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r5.claim: Maqām can function as a verbal noun and as a time or place noun; the cited examples concern standing or the circumstance of standing, not merely a residence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r5.anchor: لا يرادبه منزل إبراهيم ومقعد سليمان عليهما السلام، بل حيث كانا يقومان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r6.claim: Here maqām and nadī signify more than a home and meeting place: their grandeur, status, and abundance made them objects of boasting.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p327/r6.anchor: في موضع الفخر والمباهاة، فلا يكونان مجرد مسكن ومنزل ومجلس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses nadī as a council or gathering place and adduces a poetic line; the K and T versions add a meeting place and a place to lean.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: النادى، المجلس واستشهد له بقول الشاعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r3.claim: The form nadī is unique in the Qur'an; al-nādī occurs twice in the two verses at the end of al-Alaq.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p326/r3.anchor: وحيدة الصيغة في القرآن. وجاء النادى مرتين في آيتى

NASHR:v2p318/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p318/r8.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p318/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the mīm of خير مقاما with ḍamma; the other readers use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p318/r8.anchor: في خير مقاما فقرأ ابن كثير بضم الميم،
